$comment: Exact-phrase exceptions to the content guard (CLAUDE.md §9, §12). Every entry MUST carry a `reason` — the guard exits 1 on an entry without one. Adding an entry means a banned term is shipping to visitors, so it needs the owner's agreement, not a developer's convenience. The list stayed EMPTY through M11: the C9 disclaimer was reworded rather than excepted (docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md C9). The single entry below is a verbatim quotation of statute, which cannot be reworded without changing what a legal notice says.

$schema.phrase: Exact text that may contain a banned term. Case-insensitive. A violation is suppressed only when the match falls INSIDE an occurrence of this phrase — an allowance never disables a rule globally.
$schema.reason: Required. Why this phrase is acceptable and who agreed.
$schema.rule: Optional. Which rule id this relates to, for readers.

allow.reason: Verbatim KVKK m. 11/1-e — the statutory wording of a data-subject right, quoted in /kvkk. The blocking term exists to stop efficacy claims ("lekeleri yok eder"); paraphrasing a right in an aydınlatma metni would misstate the law. Scoped to this exact phrase, so any other use of the term still blocks. Recorded at M12, docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md G25.
